newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia general says army needs larger budget.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia general says army needs larger budget.

text.p: Indonesia's special forces chief Major-General Prabowo Subianto says the country's armed forces need a larger budget to improve professionalism, the official Antara news agency reported on Thursday.

"Our defence budget is still the smallest in the Southeast Asian region because indeed the government has prioritised economic development," Subianto told a conference of Indonesian social scientists in a rare public speech.
"However, a larger investment in this field is needed to raise the armed forces's professionalism," said Subianto, who is President Suharto's son-in-law.

He said Indonesia's defence budget, almost $3 billion in 1996, was between 1.3-1.6 percent of the nation's gross national product (GNP), whereas neighbouring Singapore and Malaysia spent between three and six percent of their GNP.
"The idea of the need for a larger investment in the military budget can be seen from a scientific point of view, however I'm sure economists can also understand this thing," Subianto said.

He said in the era of fast-moving globalisation Indonesian soldiers needed to be better educated and their skills upgraded in a number areas, highlighting the examples of proficiency in the use of English and computers.

Subianto, 45, was promoted last year to a two-star general after the special forces, known as Kopassus, was boosted from combat strength of 3,000 to around 4,800. He is the youngest general of his rank and military analysts say he is on a fast track to the post of the commander-in-chief of the Indonesian armed forces.
